node-1.label: A painful area on the right lateral chest present for 2 weeks

node-2.label: Patient is a woman in her 50s; she was taking prednisone 10 mg daily and had not used any topical medications

node-3.label: Previous treatments included methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, glycopyrrolate, oral antibiotics, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and topical antibiotics, all of which were unsuccessful

node-4.label: Physical examination demonstrated a large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest

why.why: Both pathologist and laboratory physician analyses continue to rank chronic refractory dermatosis as the most probable diagnosis (0.50), supported by the refractory immunosuppressed presentation and failure of multiple prior therapies. The biopsy still lacks detailed histomorphology, special stains, and immunohistochemistry, while HSV/VZV PCR, cultures, DIF, and serologies have been requested but are pending; this means tissue confirmation is not yet available but does not lower clinical suspicion. Confidence remains 0.50.

The expert analyses maintain viral/fungal skin infection at 0.35, noting that the prednisone-treated immunosuppressed state and painful crusted plaque keep infection viable. Special stains, HSV/VZV PCR, and cultures have been requested but remain pending, and DIF/serologies are also pending; until these studies return, viral/fungal infection cannot be excluded. Confidence remains 0.35.

The expert analyses continue to view cutaneous neoplasm/lymphoma as a secondary mimic (0.20). Because detailed histomorphology and immunohistochemistry are still pending in this refractory immunosuppressed patient, a neoplastic/lymphomatous process cannot be excluded. The pathologist's statement that all key diagnostic information has been requested but definitive confirmation awaits tissue workup supports keeping confidence at 0.20.

why.why: Both pathologist and laboratory physician analyses now explicitly identify refractory eczematous dermatitis as the most probable working diagnosis, refining the broader chronic refractory dermatosis category. attrs.why: Psoriasis is a common chronic dermatosis that can present as refractory erythematous plaques and may require multiple immunosuppressive agents. The patient's failed therapies including methotrexate, cyclosporine, and topical corticosteroids are consistent with difficult-to-treat psoriasis. Lichenoid dermatoses such as lichen planus can produce chronic, painful, crusted erythematous plaques and often require immunosuppressive therapy. The current frontier is too broad to guide specific management, and this candidate represents a less common but clinically relevant subcategory of chronic refractory dermatosis, especially given the need for tissue-based confirmation with detailed histomorphology.
